stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.

The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer, llama, and AI/ML ecosystem.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 and says it’s so capable that only ‘trusted cyber defenders’ can have it right now
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google has unveiled its next-generation AI model, Gemini 4 Argon.
The model boasts 'frontier performance' across complex tasks like software engineering, legal, finance, and cybersecurity.
Access to Gemini 4 is currently restricted, initially being available only to trusted cyber defenders.

stories.title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Critical vulnerability in Zimbra software is being actively exploited by attackers.
The flaw allows attackers to remotely inject operating system commands via a simple email.
This represents a severe security risk, enabling email-based remote code execution.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws' to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by modeling recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) simultaneously, rather than in isolation.
The work proposes a bounded, sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping to understand how these two efficient scaling techniques interact.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks, indicating its LLM nature.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks requiring context gathering and tool use on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory consumption.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon AI model, but you can't use it yet
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google has announced a new AI model named Gemini 4 Argon.
The new model is positioned as a successor or advancement over Gemini 3.5 Pro.
The model is not yet available for public use.

stories.title: Cogentic: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Proof Discovery
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Introduces Cogentic, a multi-agent system designed for automated proof discovery in complex mathematical problems.
Addresses the limitation of single-shot LLM generation by employing an iterative prove-verify loop.
Aims to tackle open research problems requiring exploration of multiple conjectures and long-horizon reasoning.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws,' a novel framework to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by modeling recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) simultaneously, rather than in isolation.
Suggests a new direction for efficient scaling in large language models by combining the benefits of recurrent structures and sparse activation.

stories.title: How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text
stories.author: Bradley Emi
bullet_points: A significant portion (27.5% to 31.1%) of real-world web text is becoming AI-generated, according to the study.
This 'wild' AI text is challenging because it comes from diverse models, is written for humans, and is unlabeled in pretraining data.
The research investigates the impact of this pervasive, real-world synthetic data on the pretraining process of large language models.

stories.title: EvoDuet: Bilevel Co-Evolution of Web Searching and Task Solving for Scientific Discovery
stories.author: Dongyeop Kang
bullet_points: Introduces EvoDuet, a novel bi-level optimization method for AI-driven scientific discovery.
Addresses the limitation of LLMs stalling when external knowledge is required during complex problem-solving.
Co-evolves both the solution and the necessary web search queries simultaneously, guided by an LLM's knowledge gap assessment.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws' to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by modeling recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) simultaneously, rather than in isolation.
Presents a novel, sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping to understand how these two efficient scaling techniques interact.

stories.title: How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text
stories.author: Bradley Emi
bullet_points: A significant portion (up to 31.1% by August) of real-world web text used for LLM pretraining is now AI-generated.
The study examines the impact of this 'wild' AI text—which is unlabeled and comes from diverse models—on language model training.
The research addresses the critical, emerging question of how synthetic data contamination affects the quality and behavior of large language models.

stories.title: OpenDLSS: A Vulkan Reimplementation of Nvidia's DLSS 5 Neural Rendering Network
stories.author: sagacity
bullet_points: OpenDLSS is a Vulkan-based reimplementation of Nvidia's DLSS 5 Neural Rendering Network.
This project aims to open up the technology, moving it away from proprietary Nvidia implementations.
It represents a significant effort in democratizing advanced AI upscaling techniques in graphics rendering.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: This fancy e-bike is one of the first to go semi-solid state
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: Lemmo 3, a new cargo e-bike from a German manufacturer, is highlighted for its innovative battery technology.
The bike features one of the first semi-solid state batteries in the e-bike market.
Semi-solid state batteries are noted for offering enhanced safety compared to conventional lithium-ion batteries.

stories.title: The AI Tamagotchis are coming
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Meta and OpenAI are entering the dedicated AI hardware space.
They are focusing on physical, 'cutesy' software agents, reminiscent of Tamagotchis.
This move signals a potential shift in how AI is integrated beyond traditional phones and computers.

stories.title: Returning from vacation? The government can search your phone without a warrant.
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: The article discusses a legal loophole allowing government searches of phones without a warrant.
This exemption is referred to as the "border exemption" and pertains to cross-border activities.
It highlights a significant privacy concern regarding digital surveillance and government access.

stories.title: A local network of implants uses your body as the wiring
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: Research demonstrates the feasibility of transmitting electrical signals directly through human tissues.
This suggests the potential for using the human body as a biological conduit or wiring system.
The technology points toward advanced bio-interfacing and implantable medical devices.

stories.title: Trump plan to combat AI risks hinges on Big Tech pals policing themselves
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: The proposed strategy to mitigate AI risks relies on voluntary compliance from major technology companies.
The plan involves securing agreements from numerous AI firms to participate in self-administered safety tests.
The initiative highlights a reliance on industry self-regulation rather than stringent government mandates for AI safety.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: Investigates sensitivity of LLM predictions to task-irrelevant prompt features, even when using verifiable rewards (RLVR).
Introduces 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test how much prompt noise affects LLM reasoning.
Proposes a decoding improvement by suppressing high-drift token candidates to enhance reasoning accuracy.

stories.title: ViTeX-Bench: Benchmarking High-Fidelity Video Scene Text Editing
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The paper introduces ViTeX-Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating high-fidelity video scene text editing.
Video scene text editing involves replacing text on surfaces (like signs or labels) while maintaining scene dynamics and motion.
This research addresses a gap in video generation technology, where precise local editing remains underdeveloped compared to image editing.

stories.title: WorldAuditBench: Interactive 3D World Auditing with Multimodal Agents
stories.author: Shiyu Chang
bullet_points: Introduces WorldAuditBench, a new framework for auditing interactive 3D simulated worlds.
Aims to automate the detection of anomalies (e.g., floating objects, inconsistent geometry) in 3D environments.
Leverages multimodal AI systems, specifically VLMs and VLAs, to perform complex 3D world inspection.

stories.title: MatLoom: Layered Text-to-Material Generation in a Compact Program Space
stories.author: Michael R. Lyu
bullet_points: Introduces MatLoom, a new language for text-to-material generation.
MatLoom generates not just appearance, but also the underlying construction rules for materials.
It uses a layer-oriented approach with shared spatial expressions to explicitly define PBR channels and patterns.

stories.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: DynaHarness addresses the challenge of long-horizon robot manipulation by bridging the gap between high-level semantic reasoning and low-level physical execution.
The system integrates pretrained robot policies as action priors, improving the efficiency of learning.
It introduces a 'dynamic physical harness' using a shared execution contract to guide self-evolution based on episode failures.

stories.title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
stories.author: Emmanuel Abbé
bullet_points: The evolution of autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE) agents is trending towards complex 'harnesses' (multi-agent orchestrators, retrieval subagents).
This complexity is driven by stagnation in progress and limitations in current Large Language Model (LLM) primitives.
The paper discusses the trade-off between using elaborate agent harnesses versus employing more primitive but highly capable coding agents.

stories.title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
stories.author: Jiayun Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in clinical AI: standard accuracy metrics fail with imbalanced medical data.
Proposes optimizing Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) using AUROC instead of simple accuracy for better clinical relevance.
Focuses on 'Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization' as a novel technique to improve MLLM performance in diagnostic tasks.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: Investigates sensitivity of LLM reasoning to task-irrelevant prompt features, even with verifiable rewards (RLVR).
Uses 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test how minor prompt changes affect LLM output while preserving the core problem.
Proposes a decoding improvement—suppressing high-drift token candidates—to enhance LLM reasoning accuracy.

stories.title: Removing Timing Shortcuts Improves Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text
stories.author: Oiwi Parker Jones
bullet_points: The study challenges recent claims of significant improvements in non-invasive brain-to-text decoding.
It suggests that reported gains might be artifacts of methodological shortcuts, specifically fixed-length window segmentation.
The research implies that the current state-of-the-art methods may be overstating their true performance without specific brain data.

stories.title: Image Classifiers are Efficient Self-Supervised Video Representation Learners
stories.author: Abir Das
bullet_points: Introduces VideoMSN, a Masked Siamese Network for efficient self-supervised spatio-temporal video representation learning.
Avoids computationally heavy 3D architectures and reconstruction-based autoencoders.
Repurposes standard image Vision Transformers by treating videos as 'super images' composed of sampled frames.

stories.title: Is Weight Tying Still Beneficial for Decoder-Only LLMs in Private Settings Under DP-SGD?
stories.author: Razane Tajeddine
bullet_points: Investigates the impact of weight tying in decoder-only LLMs when trained using Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD).
Addresses a gap in current research regarding the performance and benefits of weight tying specifically within privacy-preserving fine-tuning contexts.
Examines whether the parameter efficiency and performance gains of weight tying persist or change under DP-SGD constraints.

stories.title: Compression Footprints as Security Signals for Model-Poisoning Defense in Federated Learning
stories.author: William Eiers
bullet_points: Proposes using 'compression footprints' as a novel security signal in Federated Learning (FL) to detect model poisoning.
Challenges the conventional approach of treating lossy compression solely as an error source in FL.
The method leverages how lossy compression distorts and alters attack-generated updates differently than honest ones.

stories.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: DynaHarness addresses the challenge of long-horizon robot manipulation by bridging semantic reasoning and physical execution.
It proposes a dynamic physical harness that uses a shared execution contract to couple high-level reasoning with low-level physical control.
The system aims to improve robot learning by providing better guidance from episode failures to system component revisions.

stories.title: Looped Diffusion Transformer
stories.author: Gao Huang
bullet_points: Proposes 'Looped Diffusion Transformer' as an alternative scaling method for text-to-image models.
Increases computational depth by repeatedly running shared Transformer blocks within each denoising step, keeping parameters fixed.
Aims to enable iterative refinement of internal representations without needing explicit reasoning tokens.

stories.title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
stories.author: Jiayun Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in clinical AI: standard accuracy metrics fail with imbalanced medical datasets.
Proposes optimizing Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) using AUROC, a ranking-aware metric, instead of simple accuracy.
Focuses on prompt optimization techniques to improve the clinical utility and robustness of MLLMs in diagnosis.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: Investigates prompt sensitivity in Large Language Models (LLMs) despite advancements in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
Uses 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test how LLM predictions react to task-irrelevant prompt features.
Proposes that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding can enhance the reasoning accuracy of LLMs.

stories.title: MatLoom: Layered Text-to-Material Generation in a Compact Program Space
stories.author: Michael R. Lyu
bullet_points: Introduces MatLoom, a new compact, layer-oriented language for text-to-material generation.
The system generates not just appearance, but also the underlying construction rules for materials.
It utilizes pretrained language models and alpha-masked layers to explicitly define dependencies between patterns, color, and PBR channels.

stories.title: Linguistic Loopholes in LLM Unlearning: From a 174-Language Benchmark to Coverage-Aware Unlearning
stories.author: Abhay Yadav
bullet_points: Identifies a critical 'cross-lingual loophole' in LLM unlearning, where forgetting a fact in one language doesn't guarantee removal in others.
Proposes 'language budgeted multilingual unlearning' as a scalable solution to avoid the impracticality of unlearning across every language.
Addresses the trade-off between complete knowledge removal and preserving unrelated model capabilities during the unlearning process.

stories.title: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents
stories.author: Jing Yu Koh
bullet_points: Computer Use Agents (CUAs) are showing impressive performance, sometimes exceeding human capabilities on complex tasks.
A major hurdle for CUA adoption is their current speed and operational cost.
The paper introduces 'cua-speedrun' to provide standardized and reproducible benchmarking for CUA speed.

stories.title: Comparison of techniques for fine-tuning open-weight models for entity extraction from radiology reports
stories.author: Hari Trivedi
bullet_points: The research compares fine-tuning an open-weight model (Gemma-3-12B) against proprietary models (like GPT-4o) for entity extraction from radiology reports.
The goal addresses real-world clinical challenges: structuring free-text reports for cohort building while mitigating privacy and cost concerns associated with proprietary APIs.
The study specifically tests the model's performance in multi-label intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) acuity extraction from head-CT reports.

stories.title: Do Not Let Your AI Go Rogue, Guard Against Agentic Misalignment
stories.author: reclusivecoder
bullet_points: The article addresses the critical issue of AI agentic misalignment and the risk of AI going rogue.
It references a specific experiment where OpenAI's o1-preview was tested against Stockfish in chess.
The topic is highly relevant to current concerns regarding advanced AI safety and control mechanisms.

stories.title: Recursive self-improvement: what Google's Dream-RSI paper really does
stories.author: axrisi
bullet_points: The article analyzes Google's 'Dream-RSI' paper concerning Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).
It delves into the technical nuances of RSI, specifically discussing concepts like feedback loops and stagnation points.
The piece offers a critical perspective, questioning whether the paper's findings represent a true 'takeoff' scenario.
